program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive in execution: it accepts the support’s generic claim that a frog is “inside” without resolving the visible placement. In the edited image, one frog is clearly in the bowl, while others are on the raised lid and floor; the source bowl already contains a small dark object, so distinguish the added frog from that pre-existing detail and distinguish bowl-interior placement from merely being on the toilet. Preserve the rubric’s completion/partial/no/unknown distinctions: a verified frog in the bowl supports completion, whereas frogs only on the lid or nearby support progress at most, not completion. Make the binding and evidence criterion explicitly require checking the frog’s position relative to the bowl opening/interior, and ensure the completion decision is grounded in that visual evidence rather than inheriting an unqualified support pass. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not proof that the visible bowl frog is absent; do not force partial solely to match it. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated here—the trace is valid and queried—so investigate the semantic criterion/evidence mismatch and its calibration.
s2: The binding is too vague and the support criterion conflicts with the rubric: it asks whether there is “any progress,” yet explicitly treats a frog clearly inside the bowl as complete. Make this node assess only incomplete progress, with a separate completion path for a frog visibly placed within the bowl opening/interior. Require evidence to distinguish bowl interior from the raised lid, tank, and nearby floor, and compare against the source image so the pre-existing dark object in the bowl is not mistaken for the added frog. In this edit, frogs appear on the tank, lid, inside the bowl, and floor; the bowl frog is visible inside the opening, so do not classify the scene as merely partial progress or infer completion from an unqualified support pass. Preserve unknown when placement or identity is genuinely unclear. The trace is valid and queried, so this is a semantic criterion/routing and evidence-grounding issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; do not force the aggregate reference label.
s1: The node’s binding is malformed and underspecified (“inside (...) inside”), and its pass criterion only checks for a frog in the bowl. That criterion is satisfied by the edited image: a clearly visible green frog is positioned within the bowl opening, while other frogs are on the raised lid and floor; the small dark object in the source bowl is pre-existing and should not be mistaken for an added frog. Do not weaken the requested completion check or force the aggregate reference label of partial: the rubric says a verified requested change is complete, and this image appears to show it. Instead, make the binding and evidence explicitly identify the requested added frog by comparison with the source and verify its position relative to the bowl opening/interior, distinguishing it from frogs merely on the lid, tank, or nearby floor. Investigate why the aggregate reports partial despite this valid, high-confidence pass—especially whether this support node is being routed or interpreted as a partial-progress signal rather than completion evidence. Preserve unknown for genuinely ambiguous identity or placement. The trace is valid and queried; this is a semantic/routing or aggregation mismatch, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure.

semantic_rejection.reason: The fulfillment readout is image-free and preserves the rubric’s yes/no/partial/unknown meanings, but the saved checks do not reliably establish whether the frog is inside the toilet bowl. The completion check asks about the bowl, while the original request only says “in the toilet”; the program narrows that to “inside the toilet bowl” and binds it to the toilet in the input image. The progress check also excludes a frog already inside the bowl from partial progress, so when completion is unknown it cannot establish partial progress for that case. These are unsupported interpretations and leave a requested outcome unresolved on some paths.
semantic_rejection.source_clause: Put a frog in the toilet
semantic_rejection.counterexample: A frog visibly placed in the toilet tank or elsewhere within the toilet could satisfy the original request but fail the bowl-only completion check. If the completion check is unknown and the progress check reports no partial attempt, the program may return no or unknown despite evidence that some requested change has progressed; the saved checks do not preserve the original rubric’s progress distinction for that case.
